hero_pain: Beauty brands on Shopify lose sales and margin to influencer-driven demand spikes they didn't see coming and to expired shade inventory that couldn't sell fast enough before the next launch.
hero_intro: Beauty and cosmetics brands on Shopify operate in one of the most unpredictable demand environments in e-commerce — a single influencer post can drive a month of sales in 48 hours, while a formula discontinuation leaves dead stock across every shade in the range. Verve AI gives beauty brand operators demand forecasting and purchase order automation that handles the speed and SKU complexity of the beauty category.

pain_points.title: Influencer Demand Spikes
pain_points.description: When a beauty product goes viral, Shopify inventory disappears in days. Without real-time demand sensing and fast reorder triggering, brands lose the peak sales window entirely — and the spike is over before replacement stock arrives from their manufacturer.

pain_points.title: Short Shelf Life & Expiry Risk
pain_points.description: Cosmetics and skincare products have regulated shelf lives. Over-buying a shade or formula that falls out of trend means stock sits until it expires, forcing write-offs that can erase months of margin on that SKU entirely.

pain_points.title: High SKU Count Across Shades
pain_points.description: A single lip colour in 30 shades creates 30 individual demand signals to manage. Most beauty brands track this in spreadsheets, which means slow-moving shades stay on order while fast-moving ones stockout — all within the same product.

pain_points.title: New Launch Demand Uncertainty
pain_points.description: A brand-new SKU has no sales history to forecast from, yet the initial stock order has to be placed before launch day based on little more than a guess. Getting it wrong either strands cash in unsold launch inventory or means selling out within hours of the biggest marketing push the product will ever get.

pain_points.title: Formula Reformulation & Discontinuation Waste
pain_points.description: When a formula is updated or a line is discontinued, every unit of the old version on hand becomes obsolete almost overnight. Without advance planning, brands are left holding stock that can no longer be sold at full price, or sometimes sold at all.

pain_points.title: Gifting & Bundle Set Seasonality
pain_points.description: Q4 and Valentine's Day gift sets consume individual component SKUs at a completely different rate than those products sell standalone, and sets typically need to be pre-built weeks ahead of the season. Getting the component mix wrong means a popular set sells out while its individual pieces sit in stock.

feature_mapping.description: Verve AI monitors your Shopify sales velocity hour by hour, detecting when a product's sell rate accelerates significantly above its normal pattern. The moment a spike is detected, the system recalculates your days of cover and triggers a reorder alert — so you can act within hours rather than discovering the problem when you're already out of stock.

Verve AI forecasts sell-through timelines against product shelf life, flagging any SKU where projected demand won't clear the current stock before expiry. This lets you adjust buy quantities before placing the next purchase order, run targeted promotions on at-risk stock, or dial back production on slow shades — protecting margins before the write-off happens.

Verve AI forecasts demand at the individual shade and variant level across your entire beauty catalogue. Rather than spreading a product-level forecast evenly across shades, the system tracks each shade's own velocity curve and generates separate reorder recommendations — so your bestselling shades never stockout while slow ones stop being over-ordered.

Verve AI estimates initial launch inventory by comparing a new SKU against the early sales curves of similar past launches in your catalogue, factoring in category, price point, and planned marketing spend. Once real sales data starts coming in, the forecast recalibrates within days rather than waiting for a full sales cycle to complete.

Verve AI lets you flag a SKU as being phased out ahead of time, so the forecast automatically tapers recommended reorder quantities toward zero as the transition date approaches, instead of continuing to suggest restocking a formula you're about to retire — reducing the stranded stock left over when the new version launches.

Verve AI decomposes gift set and bundle sales back into their individual component SKUs, so a component's forecast reflects both its standalone sales and its consumption inside every set it's part of — and flags the pre-build lead time needed to have sets ready before Q4 or Valentine's Day demand hits.

social_proof_quote: An influencer featured one of our serums on a Tuesday night and we were out of stock by Thursday morning — since installing Verve AI, a spike like that now triggers an automatic reorder alert within two hours and we've never missed a window like that again.

faq.question: How does Verve AI handle demand spikes caused by influencer content or viral moments?
faq.answer: Verve AI monitors sales velocity on your Shopify store in real time and flags when a product's sell rate is significantly above its baseline. When a spike is detected, the system immediately recalculates how many days of cover you have remaining and generates an alert with a recommended emergency reorder quantity. This means you can respond within hours of a viral moment rather than discovering the stockout the next morning when orders have already been lost.

faq.question: Can Verve AI forecast at the shade level for a product with 20 or 30 colour variants?
faq.answer: Yes. Verve AI forecasts each shade and variant as an individual SKU, so each one gets its own demand signal and reorder recommendation rather than sharing a blended forecast across the product. In practice, this means your bestselling nudes and core shades get correctly sized reorders while your limited-edition shades — which sell at a fraction of the rate — don't get over-ordered into dead stock. This is one of the most common sources of margin loss for multi-shade beauty brands.

faq.question: How does Verve AI help prevent cosmetics expiry write-offs?
faq.answer: Verve AI tracks the projected sell-through rate for each SKU against the remaining shelf life of current stock. If the forecast shows a product won't clear before expiry, the system surfaces it as an at-risk item in your dashboard before the problem becomes a write-off. You can then take action — increasing promotional spend, bundling slow sellers with bestsellers, or reducing your next reorder quantity — while you still have time to act on the information.

faq.question: We're planning a new product launch — can Verve AI help us estimate initial stock levels?
faq.answer: Yes. Verve AI's new product forecasting uses the sales curve of comparable products in your catalogue to project demand for a new launch in its first 90 days. You input the product category, price point, and any planned marketing spend, and the system estimates launch inventory requirements and reorder timing. For beauty brands that launch multiple new SKUs each season, this significantly reduces the risk of either stocking out in the first week or committing to excess inventory that won't clear.

faq.question: Does Verve AI integrate with both Shopify and WooCommerce for beauty stores?
faq.answer: Yes. Verve AI is available as a native Shopify app and as a WooCommerce plugin, so it works whichever platform your beauty store runs on. The inventory forecasting, automated purchase orders, and demand sensing features work identically on both platforms. If you operate your beauty brand across multiple channels or are considering a platform migration, Verve AI can support both simultaneously.

faq.question: How does Verve AI forecast demand for a completely new product with no sales history?
faq.answer: Verve AI compares a new launch against the early sales curves of similar products already in your catalogue — matched by category, price point, and any planned marketing spend — to estimate initial stock requirements. As soon as real orders start coming in for the new SKU, the model recalibrates against actual performance within days, so the forecast improves quickly rather than staying locked to the pre-launch estimate.

faq.question: Can Verve AI help manage inventory when we discontinue or reformulate a product?
faq.answer: Yes. You can flag a SKU as being phased out ahead of its actual discontinuation date, and Verve AI will automatically taper its recommended reorder quantities toward zero as that date approaches, rather than continuing to suggest restocking a formula you're retiring. This significantly reduces the leftover stock that typically gets stranded when a new formula launches.

faq.question: How does Verve AI handle gift sets and bundles during Q4 or Valentine's Day?
faq.answer: Verve AI decomposes gift set and bundle sales back into their individual component SKUs, so each component's forecast reflects both its standalone demand and how much of it gets consumed by every set it appears in. Because sets typically need to be pre-built ahead of the season, the forecast also accounts for the lead time required to have sets ready before Q4 or Valentine's Day demand actually hits.

faq.question: Can Verve AI account for different regional demand if we sell beauty products internationally?
faq.answer: Yes. If your Shopify setup segments sales by region or market, Verve AI can forecast demand separately for each, since shade preferences, seasonal gifting occasions, and even regulatory shelf-life requirements can differ significantly between markets. This avoids a single blended global forecast masking a shade that's a bestseller in one region and a slow mover in another.

faq.question: Does Verve AI help decide when to run a promotion to clear slow-moving shades?
faq.answer: Yes. Verve AI flags SKUs where projected sell-through won't clear current stock before expiry or before a planned reformulation, giving you visibility early enough to run a targeted promotion or bundle the slow mover with a bestseller — turning a shade that was heading toward a write-off into recovered revenue instead.
